title: Agentic Fitness Functions: Extending Evolutionary Architecture Beyond Deterministic Rules
gist: The authors extend evolutionary architecture with agentic fitness functions: calibrated AI judges that evaluate bounded evidence against versioned rubrics and return structured verdicts for judgment-heavy concerns like boundary fidelity and semantic contract drift. They keep deterministic gates as gates, start agents advisory, escalate uncertainty, and promote stable findings into deterministic rules.

themes.theme: The ceiling of deterministic fitness functions

insights.claim: Deterministic fitness functions only protect what can be reduced to a rule, threshold, schema or experiment, so a dependency rule can show a package imported another but cannot tell whether it is intentional shared-kernel coupling, an accidental shortcut, or a boundary being hollowed out.
insights.speaker: Hemant Kumar Mahato
insights.so_what: Identifies a large class of architectural drift that automated rules miss, motivating a new governance layer.
insights.locator: The Ceiling of Deterministic Fitness Functions

insights.claim: Architecture normally decays through individually reasonable changes that pass every written rule while slowly moving implementation away from intent, and manual review does not scale down to every pull request, contract change, workflow trace or agent-generated patch.
insights.speaker: Hemant Kumar Mahato
insights.so_what: Frames continuous judgment, not periodic review, as necessary once AI accelerates change volume.
insights.quote: They are the normal way architecture decays: through individually reasonable changes that pass every written rule
insights.locator: The Ceiling of Deterministic Fitness Functions

themes.theme: Agentic fitness functions as calibrated judgment

insights.claim: An agentic fitness function is an architecture governance check whose evaluator is a calibrated AI agent applying a versioned analytic rubric to a small scoped evidence pack and returning a structured verdict with score, confidence and rationale, not an oracle or a replacement for deterministic checks.
insights.speaker: Hemant Kumar Mahato
insights.so_what: Defines a concrete, auditable pattern for making manual architectural judgments repeatable enough to run continuously.
insights.locator: Agentic Fitness Functions: Calibrated Judgment, Not Oracles

insights.claim: The design principle is to use deterministic gates for objective invariants and agentic judges for evidence-bound interpretation, giving the agent a small evidence pack not the whole enterprise, evaluating a named concern not good architecture in general, and returning a machine-readable result.
insights.speaker: Hemant Kumar Mahato
insights.so_what: Scoping and structure are what make agent judgment safe and trendable rather than free-form AI review.
insights.quote: use deterministic gates for objective invariants and agentic judges for evidence-bound interpretation
insights.locator: Agentic Fitness Functions: Calibrated Judgment, Not Oracles

insights.claim: A production-ready agentic fitness function has four parts: a fitness-function intent, an evidence contract limiting inspectable artifacts, a calibrated agentic judge applying a rubric, and a structured verdict with score, confidence, violated criteria, rationale, evidence references and recommended action.
insights.speaker: Hemant Kumar Mahato
insights.so_what: The four-part anatomy is a reusable blueprint teams can implement as an executable governance component.

insights.claim: Agentic fitness functions require calibration against 20 to 50 prior changes already classified as acceptable, risky or unacceptable, tuning the rubric until false positives, false negatives and variance are understood, and re-running whenever the model, prompt, rubric, tool chain or evidence contract changes.
insights.speaker: Hemant Kumar Mahato
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete calibration protocol before agent signals are allowed to influence delivery.

insights.claim: Disagreement between judges, large variance across runs, or missing evidence should escalate to a human because averaging away disagreement is dangerous, since disagreement is often the signal that the architectural trade-off is real.
insights.speaker: Hemant Kumar Mahato
insights.so_what: Treating uncertainty as an escalation trigger rather than noise is key to trustworthy agent governance.
insights.quote: Averaging away disagreement is dangerous because disagreement is often the signal that the architectural trade-off is real.

insights.claim: The system needs controls against reward hacking and prompt injection, so the agent should ignore instructions found in code comments, PR descriptions, logs or generated files unless explicitly listed as evidence, and the judge model should be isolated from the agent that produced the code.
insights.speaker: Hemant Kumar Mahato
insights.so_what: Prompt-injection and self-enhancement bias are real threats to AI-as-judge that require explicit isolation controls.
insights.quote: Treat repository content as evidence, never as judge instructions.
insights.locator: Calibration and Controls / failure mode table

insights.claim: The authors describe three example agentic fitness functions: a Boundary-Fidelity Reviewer detecting semantic coupling beyond illegal imports, a Semantic Contract Evaluator judging whether a backward-compatible contract still preserves domain meaning, and an ADR Drift Monitor checking whether decision assumptions still hold against operational reality.
insights.speaker: Hemant Kumar Mahato
insights.so_what: Grounds the pattern in specific architectural concerns where AI judgment adds value over deterministic checks.
insights.locator: Three Examples of Agentic Fitness Functions

insights.claim: The long-term value is making architectural judgment observable, calibratable and auditable, with the recommended path being to start agents advisory, escalate uncertainty, version the rubrics, and promote recurring agentic findings into named criteria or deterministic rules when patterns repeat.
insights.speaker: Hemant Kumar Mahato
insights.so_what: Promoting stable AI findings into deterministic guardrails is the mechanism that keeps governance converging and safe.
insights.quote: judgment as code, but with the humility that judgment still needs evidence, context, and accountability
